Part 1

How is a process unit engineered?

Part 1 · the plan

Five phases, each closed by a gate

  1. Phases and gatesFEED, detailed engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning
  2. The deliverable tree27 documents in 8 disciplines

Step 1 · interactive · phases

Who issues what, and what closes each phase?

Step 2 · interactive · deliverable tree

Which documents does each discipline issue?

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • FEED fixes the process and the cost; detailed engineering produces what is built; commissioning proves it.
  • Each phase ends at a gate: investment decision, delivery, mechanical completion, ready for start-up.
  • The ACU set holds 27 documents; mechanical datasheets are the largest group (11).

Where do the 124 queries come from?

Click a bar.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • Progress weights each document by its hours: one P&ID set counts more than two project registers.
  • All 27 documents are issued at Rev 0: 8410 h of 8410 h, 100 %.
  • The query log is open: HAZOP recommendations (29) and safety-layer additions (23) are the largest sources.

What do the engineering queries teach?

Part 3 · the plan

Two documents that disagree

  1. Compare two numbersthe same quantity in two documents
  2. The life of a queryraised, answered, revised, closed
  3. Checks of the registercomputed in the page, one still ✗

Step 1 · interactive · inconsistencies

Which two documents disagree, and by how much?

Step 2 · interactive · life of a query

How does EQ-em-01 get closed?

Step 3 · checks

Is the register itself consistent?

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • A query puts two documents side by side: V-4 design 200 kPa g against PSV-102 set 350 kPa g.
  • Inconsistencies are kept visible: they are the lessons of the document set.
  • A query closes only when every document it names is revised and re-issued.

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Know which phase issues a document before you trust its numbers.

2

Measure progress in earned hours, not in documents counted.

3

Compare the same quantity in two documents; raise a query when they differ.

4

Close a query only when every document it names is revised.
